points.why: It contrasts S1 0.05 with ST 0.44, attributes the ~0.39 gap to interaction probably with churn, suggests S2 to confirm, and says not to fix ad response, though it doesn't cite churn's matching gap.
It calls churn the clear top driver and price sensitivity the only fixable input, but never says to measure churn first and suggests ad response information may be worth the most.
It notes S1 sums to ~0.60 so ~40% is interaction, but doesn't say a one-at-a-time swing near the guesses would miss it.
It recommends analysing against the $2M threshold (P(revenue > $2M), indicator Sobol), explains that variance differs from decision risk, and says to check the bootstrap confidence intervals.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects fixing ad response because ST, not S1, is the relevant test.

notes: The sentence 'little effect at low churn, but a large one when churn is high or low' is self-contradictory and muddles the interaction explanation.
